processing: Tender shoots are shaped into a slightly flat, straight leaf resembling a sparrow's tongue.
harvest_season: Spring is usual for this style of bud-and-leaf green. Gardens are reported at around 1000 m, give or take 200 m.
appearance_dry: Slightly flat, slender, jade-green leaves shaped like a sparrow's tongue, with silver down.
appearance_wet: Tender green shoots that open into small, whole clusters.
taste_profile: Mellow, clean and sweet, with a tall, lingering aroma.

brewing.notes: These are general settings for a tender flat green. A glass lets you watch the shoots stand and open.

vintage_note: It is normally sold as the current spring tea, and as with other greens it fades within about a year. It may be packaged under the wider Hanzhong Xianhao name, so look for Ningqiang as the origin, plus a harvest date.
description:
Ningqiang Queshe is a flat green tea from Ningqiang county at the southwestern edge of Hanzhong, in southern Shaanxi. Queshe means sparrow's tongue, a common name in Chinese tea for small pointed shoots, and this one pairs that shape with the name of its county.

The leaf is slim, slightly flat and silver-downed, in a bright jade green. Gardens are reported at around 1000 metres, and the finished tea keeps its shoots whole and tender.

The cup is bright green with a tall aroma and a mellow, sweet taste. Keep the water cool and the steeps measured, as with any shoot-rich green, since heat turns the sweetness flat.

The name exists both on its own and inside the Hanzhong Xianhao family. Queshe is also a general shape name used in other provinces, so check that the county is really Ningqiang.
history:
Lu Yu's Classic of Tea lists the Jinniu area, which is today's Ningqiang, among the tea-growing places of Liangzhou, so tea here has a Tang record. The named tea is far newer: it was developed in 1993 and passed a quality assessment by the Tea Research Institute of the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences in 1997.

In 2005 Hanzhong kept it as one of three leading local brands, then in 2007 folded all three into the single Hanzhong Xianhao name. Output has been put at about 500 tonnes a year.
